recipe.notes:
Pointwise reranker; one raw logit (vocabulary position 0 at the final position) per document, no sigmoid/softmax. The score template puts the document before the query, so both the query and the trailing " ??" sit at the tail: the anchor is last, and the client's cut reserves every fixed token and re-attaches the frame -- the paper's in-process path instead right-truncates the whole prompt at 8192 (declared above as the reference's known deviation over the cap; the untruncated long-document prompt of the measurement made when the recipe was written is ~14.0k tokens, 14,037 ids for this checkpoint). template.jinja (the one family-wide template name) renders in the engine's context (vLLM's /rerank passes two messages, roles query and document) and in the CPU harness's context (flat query/document kwargs). Like the 1b and 2b templates it has no instruction slot: the vendor template's inline " {instruction}" (read from a kwarg or a system message) is dropped, because the client declares instruction: none and a pairs row's instruction is ignored on both sides (neither folded nor appended).
reference.py keeps the paper's own prompt construction and score path; its prompt builder takes no instruction (the paper's factory never set one; this recipe's mode is none). Its render mode fills the harness's rerank span format with the paper's own spans -- the raw query and the raw documents its prompt builder receives, uncut -- and never reproduces the client's cut (neither the settle rule nor the anchor-preserving content cut): under the cap and within the share they equal the wire's spans byte for byte. Declared divergence rows and the pairs-file rule: an over-share query (over 4096 tokens and under the pair budget) is a declared divergence row -- the wire ships the query settled at its share, the reference keeps it whole -- and an over-cap pair is the declared anchor_drop_over_cap row; the gating pairs therefore keep queries within the share and documents within the budget.
Serving needs no plugin and no image change: the architecture override, the template file and the pooler config suffice, and the engine's tokenizer-mode stays auto (never --tokenizer-mode mistral: vLLM's cross-encoder processor refuses the mistral-common tokenizer, and the HF tokenizer.json is what the paper's reference reads with use_fast=True). Numerics: bfloat16 weights; vLLM's pooling score head defaults to fp32 while the reference computes the whole model in bf16 -- bounded by the raw-logit gate, and --hf-overrides '{"head_dtype": "model"}' is the closer-to-reference fallback if the GPU wave's logit gate ever fails (not measured on CPU: the 14.9 GB weights are the GPU wave's). The GPU wave must check: the raw-logit scale of the served scores (the card's example logits should reproduce, not their sigmoid), the 8192 budget with the 4096-token query share on over-budget pairs, and stage 1's /tokenize agreement (R29).
